headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Authelia can egress broadly while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, but no shared workspace or direct interaction is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser path is documented between authelia and nuwa-skill. Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, while nuwa-skill only shows allowlisted egress; neither profile shows it ingesting the other’s outputs by default. The interaction is therefore not plausibly established from the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess prompt-injection risk.
IF nuwa-skill begins parsing Authelia-generated text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue.
Route inter-agent data through a structured JSON schema.
Add provenance tags to all exchanged content.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and can handle authentication flows, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. No sensitive data classes are listed for either agent, and no shared workspace or OAuth principal is documented. Leakage is possible only if operators co-locate data or connect them to the same secrets-bearing workflow.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same secrets-bearing workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is granted access to PHI, financial data, or secrets, reassess to a higher severity.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in a shared directory.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
Restrict Authelia egress to required IdP endpoints only.
Review logs for accidental payload capture.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls and nuwa-skill can also egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable resource access. Without a shared writable surface or concurrency primitive, direct capability conflict is limited to network contention, which is small and avoidable.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict severity increases.
IF an orchestrator introduces shared mutable state without locking, reassess upward.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid shared git branches for both agents.
Serialize any writes through one coordinator.
Check for accidental concurrent jobs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can produce authentication-related outputs, and nuwa-skill could consume them, but no verification step or downstream action authority is documented. The pairwise risk is that nuwa-skill may treat Authelia output as authoritative if wired together, creating a default-path cascade once integrated, though this is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill is configured to act on Authelia outputs without validation, cascading error becomes active.
IF Authelia output is used as a source of facts for downstream actions, reassess to high.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actioning outputs.
Require schema validation on exchanged messages.
Log source provenance alongside each claim.
Limit downstream actions to read-only mode.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no touched data classes, so there is no documented residency or regulated-data mismatch. Authelia’s broad egress and nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress create a compliance gap only if operators route regulated data through them; that pathway is not present in the profiles, so the risk stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent’s workflow, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF deployment policy requires a specific DPA or HIPAA boundary, verify both agents against it.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Use region-restricted endpoints where possible.
Review vendor terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
